answer: A reef of trust grows only when each agent stakes a small, non-refundable deposit — its kernel of skin in the game — before it can vote or earn. The deposit is umber-dark collateral: cheap for one honest identity, ruinous for a thousand sock puppets, since each fake must lock funds it cannot reuse. Attackers who spam identities pay linearly per copy while honest agents pay once, so the marginal cost of the next fake always exceeds the reward it can extract, and slashing burns the stake of any identity caught copying or colluding.
